title: Mango (Raw-Ripe): modeled ₹677/qtl left, Athirampuzha → Angamaly
summary: February 2023: reported mango (Raw-Ripe) prices at Athirampuzha and Angamaly imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 75% of 16 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹677 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 40 same-variety market pairs screened for mango (Raw-Ripe) in February 2023; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Mango - Raw-Ripe, FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Angamaly report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: February 2023
scenes.caption: Athirampuzha (Kerala) and Angamaly (Kerala) both reported mango (Raw-Ripe) prices for the same variety and grade (Mango - Raw-Ripe, FAQ) on 16 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Athirampuzha reported a median ₹5,400 per quintal. Angamaly reported a median ₹7,000 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,350/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,350 per quintal, and Angamaly was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 78 km by road
scenes.caption: 78 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~1 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹17/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹516 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹209 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Angamaly report, the rule selects 15 of 16 modeled shipping days. 12 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹677 per quintal (₹326 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Mango (Raw-Ripe) route from Athirampuzha to Angamaly was positive on 75% of matched days in February 2023. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹67,700, or ₹32,600 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to mango (Raw-Ripe)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹17/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Mango (Raw-Ripe) route from Athirampuzha to Angamaly was positive on 75% of matched days in February 2023. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹67,700, or ₹32,600 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

sources.title: Agmarknet / data.gov.in daily mandi modal prices (retained AGRINET snapshot)
RBI Working Paper WPS (DEPR) 08/2024 — Price Dynamics of Tomato, Onion and Potato
